_readme: Rules the Compliance agent (engine/policy/compliance.py) checks a plan against. Each rule names its jurisdiction, the requirement in plain words, how it is checked (a function in engine/policy/compliance.py), and its source. A rule that applies to one channel says so. This is a rules engine, not legal advice: requirements were read from the sources on the date in checked_on; laws change. Add a rule by appending an object with a check that exists in engine/policy/compliance.py CHECKS.

rules.requirement: Gmail and Yahoo require bulk senders' marketing mail to carry one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058) plus a visible unsubscribe link, honored within two days, and to keep user-reported spam under 0.3% (Gmail's target is under 0.1%).
rules.confirm: One-click unsubscribe is a header your platform adds: confirm it is on (engine/deliverability/analyze.py checks it in real headers).

rules.requirement: Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft (Outlook.com, Hotmail.com and Live.com since 5 May 2025) require senders of more than 5,000 messages a day to pass SPF and DKIM and publish DMARC (p=none or stricter) aligned with one of them; Microsoft sends failing mail to junk, then rejects it with 550 5.7.515.
rules.confirm: Run lcm "check deliverability for <your sending domain>" (engine/deliverability/dns_collect.py) and resolve anything RED before launch.

rules.id: suppression of opt-outs, bounces and complaints
rules.requirement: Never mail people who unsubscribed, hard bounced or complained.
Commercial email must include the sender's valid physical postal address (a registered PO box or private mailbox counts).
Commercial email must offer a clear way to opt out that keeps working for at least 30 days after the send, honored within 10 business days.
Subject lines and header information must not mislead.
A commercial message must be identified as an advertisement unless the recipient gave prior affirmative consent to receive it.
rules.confirm: Confirm every recipient opted in to marketing email, or add a clear advertisement disclosure.

rules.requirement: Marketing texts only between 8 a.m. and 9 p.m. at the recipient's location.
Marketing texts need the recipient's prior express written consent and an opt-out.

States set narrower windows than the TCPA: Connecticut 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. (texts covered); Oregon 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. (texts covered from 1 January 2026); Florida, Oklahoma and Maryland 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.; Texas 9 a.m. to 9 p.m., noon on Sundays. Recipient state is not known per person, so the send hour must fall inside 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. local, and a send before noon is flagged for Sundays. These are the state rules this file tracks, not every state's.
rules.unconfirmed: Whether the Florida, Maryland, Oklahoma and Texas hour limits reach texts as well as calls is not settled; they are applied anyway.

rules.requirement: Texas limits telephone solicitation to noon to 9 p.m. on Sundays, and several other states restrict Sunday solicitation further or ban it; whether those rules reach texts is not settled.
rules.confirm: Decide with counsel whether marketing texts skip Sundays (most ESPs can exclude a weekday from a flow's send window).

rules.requirement: Oregon (texts covered), Florida, Oklahoma and Maryland limit marketing contacts on the same subject to three per 24 hours.

rules.id: state texting consent and opt-out records
rules.requirement: Florida's Telephone Solicitation Act covers texts and requires a STOP reply to be honored; Washington bars commercial texts to Washington numbers without consent; Virginia requires a STOP or UNSUBSCRIBE reply to be honored for at least 10 years.
rules.confirm: Confirm SMS opt-outs are kept for at least 10 years and never re-opted in by a later import.

rules.requirement: Commercial electronic messages need express or implied consent.
rules.confirm: Implied consent expires: two years after a purchase, six months after an inquiry or application. Exclude Canadian records whose implied consent has lapsed, or confirm they gave express consent.

rules.requirement: Messages must identify the sender, give contact information and a no-cost unsubscribe mechanism, honored within 10 business days.
Every message identifies who sent it and on whose behalf, with a mailing address and a phone number, email or web address that stays valid for 60 days.

Marketing email to individuals needs specific consent, or the soft opt-in for people who bought or negotiated to buy a similar product and were offered an opt-out at collection and in every message. The ICO is revising this guidance after the Data (Use and Access) Act.
rules.confirm: Confirm each UK record has consent or qualifies for the soft opt-in.

rules.requirement: Marketing email needs prior consent, except to existing customers for similar products with an opt-out at collection and in every message (ePrivacy Directive, article 13).
rules.confirm: Confirm the lawful basis for each EU record and that consent records can be produced.

rules.requirement: Every marketing message offers a free, easy opt-out.

UWG section 7 requires prior express consent for marketing email; the Federal Court of Justice (I ZR 164/09) puts the burden of proof on the sender, which in practice means a stored double opt-in confirmation per person.
rules.confirm: Confirm German records were collected with double opt-in and that each confirmation is stored.

rules.id: Spam Act consent, identification and unsubscribe
rules.requirement: Commercial messages need consent, must identify the sender and offer a functional unsubscribe that keeps working for 30 days after the send, honored within 5 working days.
Every message identifies the business that authorized it.
